QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_10

question.text: Under the Logic Model, the 't0 year' refers to:

answer.text: The final year of the project when impact is measured
The year after project closure when exit protocols are triggered

The designated pre-implementation period between project listing and commencement during which beneficiary selection, manpower deployment, capacity building, participatory planning and project logistics are finalised
A tax holiday year granted under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 4.3(vi), the Logic Model mandates a time gap between project listing and implementation start — the t0 year. Activities during t0 include selection of actual beneficiaries, planning and deploying manpower, capacity building, participatory planning with the beneficiary community, and coordinating project logistics. Duration and costs of t0 must be documented at pre-listing and listing stages. **The Trap:** A confuses t0 with final year. B confuses t0 with exit phase. D is unrelated tax terminology — there is no 'tax holiday year' called t0. **Cross-Exam Context:** t0 planning is tested in XXIII Ch 3 (Project Design), Ch 7 (SAS engagement planning), and referenced in SSE-listing disclosures (III-A/III-C). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Always request the t0 work plan and budget during SIA scoping — if beneficiary selection and participatory planning were skipped, the outputs/outcomes in year 1 are likely inflated. A missing t0 is a material weakness to flag in the management representation letter.
